claim.pdf_says: 12.3.8.4   General rules   [printed as a fourth-level clause heading, in the same bold style and at the same depth as "12.3.8.3   Syntax rules" on page 335, both children of "12.3.8 REPOSITORY paragraph"]
claim.why_it_matters: Level-2 (##) makes 12.3.8.4 a SIBLING of "## 12.3.8 REPOSITORY paragraph" rather than its child, while its own sibling 12.3.8.3 on page 335 is correctly "### 12.3.8.3 Syntax rules". The heading tree therefore claims the REPOSITORY paragraph clause has no general rules and that a new top-level clause begins here, which corrupts any navigation or section-walk that resolves a spec citation by heading depth.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED. Rendered PDF pages 337 (printed folio 307) and 335 (printed folio 305) at 300 dpi and compared them against E:/Temp/specrecon/v337/page-337.md and specs/ISO_COBOL.md:14435-14599. Nothing from the PDF is missing or altered; the only difference is the count of '#' characters in an ATX marker, which the rejection criteria classify as formatting. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING - the 'kind' label is self-refuting. The heading is present verbatim with its full clause number, its exact title, and a correctly hierarchical id anchor: '' / '## 12.3.8.4 General rules' (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:14598-14599; page-337.md lines 8-9). The claim's own markdown_says field quotes the heading it calls missing. The page body is faithful too: item b) of the syntax rules, general rules 1) through 8), both continuation paragraphs under 1) and 5), and the sentence under 7) all match the render word for word. (2) THE CLAIM'S PDF EVIDENCE CARRIES NO DEPTH SIGNAL. I looked at the printed glyphs. Page 335 prints '12.3.8.3 Syntax rules' and page 337 prints '12.3.8.4 General rules' in the identical bold face, identical size, at the identical left margin. That is true - but it is true of every heading level in this standard: ISO renders 12.3.8, 12.3.8.1 and 12.3.8.4 with one bold weight and essentially one size. So 'same bold style and at the same depth' proves nothing about nesting. The only printed depth cue is the dotted number, and the transcription reproduces it exactly ('12.3.8.4'). The normative depth carrier is intact. (3) HEADING DEPTH IS NOT A HIERARCHY CARRIER ANYWHERE IN THIS TRANSCRIPTION, so nothing incremental is corrupted. Measured across the whole file: of 806 four-component headings only 24 sit at level 4 - 620 are '###' and 162 are '##'. Three-component numbers appear at levels 2, 3 and 4 (276/508/17). Level 1 ('#') is not a clause level at all: it is occupied 947 times by the injected page-break running header '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)', across 1261 page blocks. The heading tree is therefore reset to level 1 at nearly every printed page boundary already. A 'section-walk that resolves a spec citation by heading depth' is unusable on this document by construction, with or without this heading, so the stated harm does not exist. (4) NO IN-REPO CONSUMER IS AFFECTED. The repo's spec navigator, scripts/spec/extract_rule_catalog.py, matches headings with HEADING = re.compile(r"^#{2,6}\s+(?P\d+(?:\.\d+)*)\s+(?P.+?)\s*$") - deliberately level-agnostic, keying on the dotted number. Its own comment gives both shapes as normal: 'e.g. "## 8.4.3.13.3 Syntax rules" or "### 14.9.28.4 General rules"'. Citation resolution here is by clause number and by the section-N-N-N anchors, both of which are correct on page 337. (5) THE CLAIM MISDESCRIBES THE MARKDOWN. It says level 2 means 'a new top-level clause begins here'. '##' is not top-level in this file - '#' is, and it holds page furniture. '##' is also the level of the 'Page NNN' markers themselves, so a '##' clause heading is a peer of page furniture rather than a top-level clause. The inference the claim draws from the level is not the one the document's markup supports. What is genuinely true is narrower than the finding: within clause 12.3.8 the markup is internally inconsistent - .1, .2 and .3 are '###' while .4 is '##'. That is a markup inconsistency in a document whose heading levels are systematically non-hierarchical, not a discrepancy between what the PDF says and what the markdown says. No clause number, rule text, rule ordinal, choice indicator or normative word differs. Under the stated rubric - reject when the difference is only formatting and does not change meaning - this is a reject.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The heading '12.3.8.4 General rules' is transcribed verbatim with the correct clause number and a correct '<a id="section-12-3-8-4">' anchor; only the ATX level differs from its siblings ('##' at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:14599 versus '###' for 12.3.8.1/.2/.3 at :14438/:14443/:14513). If the project wants heading levels to encode hierarchy, that is one repo-wide normalization sweep keyed on the dotted-number component count - 782 of 806 four-component headings are currently at the wrong level, and 947 page-break running headers occupy level 1 and would have to be demoted first - not a page-337 finding. Note also that the claim's cited PDF evidence is inert: ISO prints 12.3.8, 12.3.8.3 and 12.3.8.4 in the same bold weight and size, so 'same bold style' distinguishes no depth; the dotted number is the only printed depth cue and it transcribed correctly.
